hints: Put both fractions over the common denominator $(1-\cos\theta)(1+\cos\theta)$.
Expand and simplify the numerator to obtain $4\cos\theta$.
walkthrough:
Combine the two fractions on the left-hand side over a common denominator:
$$\mathrm{LHS} = \frac{(1 + \cos\theta)^2 - (1 - \cos\theta)^2}{(1 - \cos\theta)(1 + \cos\theta)}$$

Expand the brackets in the numerator and simplify the difference of squares in the denominator:
$$\text{Numerator} = (1 + 2\cos\theta + \cos^2\theta) - (1 - 2\cos\theta + \cos^2\theta) = 4\cos\theta$$
$$\text{Denominator} = 1 - \cos^2\theta$$

Rewrite $\sin^2\theta$ as $\sin\theta \cdot \sin\theta$ and use $\tan\theta = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ to reach the required expression:
$$\frac{4\cos\theta}{\sin^2\theta} = \frac{4}{\sin\theta \cdot \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}} = \frac{4}{\sin\theta\tan\theta} = \mathrm{RHS}$$

ai_rubric.Trigonometric Identities: Combines fractions over $(1-\cos\theta)(1+\cos\theta)$ (M1). Simplifies numerator to $4\cos\theta$ and denominator to $\sin^2\theta$ (A1A1). Completes proof to $\frac{4}{\sin\theta\tan\theta}$ (A1).

hints: Substitute $\frac{4}{\sin\theta\tan\theta}$ in place of the bracketed expression.
Find both solutions in the 1st and 3rd quadrants ($0^\circ < \theta < 360^\circ$).
walkthrough:
Substitute the identity from part (i) into the given equation:
$$\sin\theta \left(\frac{4}{\sin\theta\tan\theta}\right) = 3$$

Cancel the $\sin\theta$ terms and solve for $\tan\theta$:
$$\frac{4}{\tan\theta} = 3 \implies \tan\theta = \frac{4}{3}$$

Find all solutions for $\theta$ in the range $0^\circ < \theta < 360^\circ$:
$$\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{3}\right) \approx 53.1^\circ$$
$$\theta = 180^\circ + 53.13^\circ \approx 233.1^\circ$$

ai_rubric.Trigonometric Equations: Substitutes part (i) identity and cancels $\sin\theta$ to get $\tan\theta = \frac{4}{3}$ (M1). Obtains $\theta = 53.1^\circ$ (A1). Obtains $\theta = 233.1^\circ$ (A1).
